A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMHNet research, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 includes supplementary Sections 7–9; the supplied v3 ends after the references. This is an observable omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Section 5 and the supplement report original MMHNet benchmark results, ablations, activation analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original MMHNet results on UnAV100, LongVale, and VGGSound, together with architectural and threshold ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same flow-matching method, non-causal Mamba-2 architecture, temporal and multimodal routing, and chunking/dechunking procedures. Clarifying that cosine similarity applies to individual q and k does not change the method. Missing supplementary implementation descriptions do not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: VGGSound training and evaluation, UnAV100 and LongVale evaluation, and short-to-long generation coverage remain. WavCaps and Clotho cease to be named because the supplement is omitted, but v3 still reports auxiliary text-to-audio training; this does not establish a change in the data actually used.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained benchmark tables and figures are unchanged. However, v1 Section 9 separately compares MMHNet with MMAudio on synthesis runtime; v3 omits this comparison. Newly cited SoundReactor and Titan-Guide are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v3 omits supplementary evaluation procedures, including timing 500-second synthesis and controlled sweeps over CFG values 2–6. The retained benchmarks keep their training duration, model configurations, and evaluation metrics. Missing dataset-construction and preprocessing descriptions are disclosure losses, not evidence that retained experiments used revised settings.

E4.justification: v3 removes the temporal-only routing comparison, condition positional-embedding ablation, similarity-function comparison, CFG sensitivity study, activation-map analysis, and runtime analysis from Section 9. Core-network, hierarchy, and threshold ablations remain in Tables 3–5; the basic no-routing versus full-routing comparison therefore survives despite Table A6 disappearing.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The omitted runtime paragraph mentions multiple samples but specifies no repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores and main result figures are unchanged, but substantial unique supplementary results disappear. These include temporal-only routing DeSync 0.474 in Table A6, positional-embedding results, Euclidean/dot-product routing results, non-default CFG results, and approximately 60 versus 120 seconds for MMHNet versus MMAudio to synthesize 500 seconds. Some default-condition rows remain duplicated in the main tables.

T1.justification: The flow-matching equations, state-space formulation, cosine routing definitions, and upsampling mathematics remain equivalent. The q/k wording clarification adds no mathematical definition or property, and the omitted supplement contains no separate proof or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: training on short clips enables long-form generation, MMHNet combines hierarchical routing with non-causal Mamba-2, and it improves long-video audio generation. Supplementary evidence is removed without narrowing these claims.

C2.justification: v3 loses supplementary interpretations linking cosine routing to CLIP embedding geometry, characterizing condition positional embeddings as having little effect, and attributing causal-Mamba behavior to early-token bias. The main explanations concerning positional encoding, non-causal processing, and long-duration alignment remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Omitting Sections 7–9 removes the auxiliary training-dataset identities, caption withholding on UnAV100, custom LongVale evaluation-set construction, AdamW learning rate and iteration budget, 25-step setting, feature-projection and VAE/STFT details, CFG choice, and runtime hardware. v3 still directs readers to supplementary setup details that are absent from the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: v3 adds SoundReactor and Titan-Guide to the multimodal-model discussion and drops appendix-only references to Clotho, WavCaps, Make-An-Audio 2, BigVGAN, and SELU. Positioning relative to MMAudio, HNet, Mamba, and long-form generation methods remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The document structure loses the entire standalone supplement covering datasets, implementation, and additional experiments, while a new acknowledgements section is added. Retained Sections 1–6 are almost verbatim, with only small wording clarifications and an author-order adjustment; the substantial change is structural omission rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure A6 and Tables A6–A9 disappear without replacement, removing the supplementary visual presentation of activation behavior and design sensitivities. Main Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–5 retain their structures and content, apart from a shortened Table 4 caption and minor text reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the core method, claims, and benchmark scores but removes essential reproduction information, including the training recipe and custom LongVale evaluation-set construction, alongside substantial supporting analyses. References to the missing supplement remain. Small wording improvements and added citations do not offset the substantial loss of reproducibility and evidential support in the supplied paper.
